subtopics.title: UN Security Council and Control Regimes
subtopics.summary: The UN Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations, established in 1945 under the UN Charter, and it has five permanent and ten non-permanent members. Its main purpose is maintaining international peace and security. Outside the Council, the Australia Group and the export control regimes NSG, MTCR and Wassenaar Arrangement work to limit the spread of dangerous weapons.
facts: UN Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the UN, established in 1945 under the UN Charter.
Permanent members (P5): China, France, Russia, USA and UK.
Ten non-permanent members; the General Assembly elects five each year for two-year terms.
Non-permanent seats are distributed on a regional basis.
UNSC presidency rotates every month among its 15 members.
UNSC headquarters: New York City; it authorises peacekeeping missions and imposes sanctions.
Coffee Club prime movers: Italy, Spain, Australia, Canada, South Korea, Argentina and Pakistan.
Coffee Club opposes expansion of permanent seats; India is a key Uniting for Consensus opponent of Germany's bid.
Australia Group founded in 1985 after chemical weapons were used in the Iran-Iraq War; India joined in 2018.
NPT adopted 1968, in force 1970, extended indefinitely 1995; North Korea withdrew in 2003.

subtopics.title: Critical Technology and Mineral Security
subtopics.summary: Pax Silica is a US-led framework to build trusted technology supply chains, covering semiconductors, AI infrastructure, critical minerals and advanced manufacturing, and India is set to join it. The Minerals Security Partnership is a US-led alliance launched in 2022, and India is the only developing country to be part of it. India's National Critical Minerals Mission and KABIL aim to secure critical mineral assets at home and abroad.
facts: Pax Silica is a US-led multilateral framework; India is set to join it.
Pax Silica scope: semiconductors and AI infrastructure, critical minerals and energy inputs, advanced manufacturing, compute and data logistics.
Pax Silica members include the US, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, UK and Israel.
Minerals Security Partnership: US-led alliance launched in 2022; India is the only developing country member.
India and US launched iCET in 2022 for semiconductors, AI and wireless communication.
National Critical Minerals Mission runs from FY 2024-25 to 2030-31; nodal ministry is Ministry of Mines.
KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Ltd) acquires exploration and exclusivity rights for five lithium brine blocks in Argentina.
Samudravaan Project explores the Indian Ocean seabed for critical minerals.
Lithium triangle: Argentina, Bolivia and Chile; top lithium reserves are Bolivia, Argentina and Chile.
India's first lithium site is Salal-Haimana (Reasi, J&K); first auctioned site is Korba (Chhattisgarh).

subtopics.title: Government Schemes and Governance Platforms
subtopics.summary: Swadesh Darshan, launched in 2015, develops theme-based tourism circuits, and its 2.0 version shifts to destination-centric and sustainable tourism. A CAG audit of PMKVY for 2015-2022 found weak planning, unspent funds, data lapses and poor placement outcomes. PMMVY is a conditional cash transfer for pregnant women and lactating mothers, while PRAGATI is a three-tier platform for monitoring projects and redressing grievances.
facts: Swadesh Darshan was launched in 2015 as a central sector scheme under the Ministry of Tourism.
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 shifts from circuit-based to destination-centric infrastructure.
PRASHAD focuses on infrastructure development at major pilgrimage and heritage sites.
CAG audit of PMKVY (2015-2022): nearly 20% of state component funds remained unspent.
PMKVY audit: about 95% of candidate records had invalid or missing information; placement rate only 41%.
PMMVY launched in 2017 as a conditional cash transfer; incorporated into Mission Shakti in 2022.
PMMVY targets pregnant women and lactating mothers aged 19 and above; Rs 5,000 for the first living child.
PRAGATI, launched in 2015, is a three-tier monitoring and grievance redressal platform.
PRAGATI integrates with CPGRAMS to address citizens' grievances.
PM SVANidhi (2020) gives affordable working capital loans to street vendors and offers a PM SVANidhi credit card.

subtopics.title: Economy, Finance and Global Rankings
subtopics.summary: India overtook Japan to become the fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP, and its growth is described as the fastest among major economies. The OECD/G20 global minimum tax framework seeks a 15% minimum effective tax rate for large multinationals. Rankings such as the Henley Passport Index 2026 and NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index measure global mobility and state-level export readiness.
facts: India overtook Japan to become the world's fourth-largest economy in nominal GDP.
Nominal GDP about $4.18 trillion; per capita nominal GDP $2,820, ranked 136th.
Real GDP growth of 8.2% in Q2 of FY2025; described as the fastest-growing major economy.
Food prices entered deflation at -0.2%, the first time since 2014.
Global minimum tax: introduced by OECD in 2021; minimum 15% effective tax rate for large MNEs.
Pillar 1 reallocates 25% of profits above a set margin to market jurisdictions.
RBI State Finances 2025-26: states' consolidated fiscal deficit rose to 3.3% of GDP in 2024-25.
Henley Passport Index 2026: India ranked 80th, up from 85th in 2025.
Export Preparedness Index (4th edition): business ecosystem carries 40% weight.
Payments Regulatory Board is chaired by the RBI Governor under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007.

subtopics.title: Defence, Diplomacy and Resources
subtopics.summary: India and Germany marked 25 years of their strategic partnership during Chancellor Friedrich Merz's first official visit to India, signing agreements on defence, trade and mobility. India and Pakistan exchange lists of their nuclear installations every year under a 1988 agreement. India became the world's largest rice producer at about 150 million tonnes, while the Indus Waters Treaty faces renewed tensions.
facts: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made his first official visit to India, marking 25 years of the strategic partnership.
Germany announced a visa-free transit facility for Indian passport holders.
Bilateral India-Germany trade crossed USD 50 billion in 2024.
DRDO partners with Europe's OCCAR for the Eurodrone MALE UAV programme.
Pinaka LRGR-120 has a range of approximately 120 km and was flight-tested at Chandipur, Odisha.
Operation Pawan: Indian peacekeeping force in Sri Lanka, launched after the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 29 July 1987.
India-Pakistan agreement on nuclear installations was signed on 31 December 1988 and entered into force on 27 January 1991.
Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960 with World Bank as broker; eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej go fully to India.
Sawalkot hydropower project on the Chenab (J&K) is a 1856 MW run-of-river project.
India surpassed China to become the world's largest rice producer (about 150 million tonnes).

quizzes.title: UN and Control Regimes Check
quizzes.passage: The United Nations Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations and was established in 1945 under the UN Charter. Its main purpose is maintaining international peace and security. It addresses countries that threaten global security, authorises peacekeeping missions and imposes sanctions. In cases of international conflict, it can also authorise the use of force. The Council has fifteen members. Five of them are permanent members: China, France, Russia, the United States and the United Kingdom. The other ten are non-permanent members, and the General Assembly elects five of them each year for a two-year term. These ten seats are distributed on a regional basis. The Council's headquarters are in New York City. Several arrangements outside the Council work to limit the spread of dangerous weapons. The Australia Group was founded in 1985 in response to the use of chemical weapons during the Iran-Iraq War, and it works to prevent the proliferation of chemical and biological weapons. Three export control regimes also operate in this field: the Nuclear Suppliers Group, the Missile Technology Control Regime and the Wassenaar Arrangement. Each of these bodies is a separate arrangement with its own membership and purpose. The booklet presents these as part of the wider international effort against weapons proliferation.

questions.q: In which year did India join the Australia Group?
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that India joined the Australia Group in 2018.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The guidelines of the Australia Group are legally binding on all its members.
Reason (R): The Australia Group is an informal multilateral arrangement and is not legally binding.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Australia Group as an informal arrangement that is not legally binding.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Nuclear Suppliers Group   ->   A. Controls conventional arms and dual-use goods
II. Missile Technology Control Regime   ->   B. Regulates nuclear-related exports
III. Wassenaar Arrangement   ->   C. Prevents spread of missile and drone technology
IV. Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty   ->   D. Classifies states by nuclear status as of 1 January 1967
questions.explanation: NSG regulates nuclear-related exports, MTCR covers missile and drone technology, Wassenaar controls conventional arms and dual-use goods, and the NPT classifies states by their 1967 nuclear status.

questions.q:
I. The Missile Technology Control Regime was set up in 1987 to prevent the spread of missile and drone technology.
II. The Australia Group has 42 member countries along with the European Union.
III. The Wassenaar Arrangement was set up before the Missile Technology Control Regime.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the Wassenaar Arrangement (1996) came after the MTCR (1987).

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the UN Security Council are correct?
I. The Council's presidency rotates among its 15 members every month.
II. The Security Council itself elects the five non-permanent members each year.
III. India served as a non-permanent member seven times before its 2021-22 term.
IV. Germany is one of the prime movers of the Coffee Club.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, II is wrong because the General Assembly elects non-permanent members, and IV is wrong because Italy, Spain and others are the prime movers.

questions.q: Which country is one of the prime movers of the Coffee Club, a group that opposes expansion of permanent seats on the UNSC?
questions.explanation: Italy is listed among the prime movers of the Coffee Club, which opposes expansion of permanent seats.

questions.q: In which year was the Wassenaar Arrangement established?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Wassenaar Arrangement to 1996.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty was extended indefinitely in 1995.
II. North Korea remains a member of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: North Korea withdrew from the NPT in 2003, so only statement I is correct.

quizzes.title: Economy and Rankings Check
quizzes.passage: India has climbed several global economic rankings in recent years. It overtook Japan to become the fourth-largest economy measured by nominal GDP, and it is projected to move ahead of another major economy to take third place. Its growth is described as the fastest among major economies, supported by strong domestic demand and a services-led model. Services form the largest share of the economy, followed by industry and agriculture. Food prices also entered a phase of deflation, meaning a sustained fall in the general price level. The Reserve Bank of India reported that states' consolidated fiscal deficit rose to 3.3 per cent of GDP in 2024-25. Rankings also measure other aspects of national standing. The Henley Passport Index ranks passports by the number of destinations that holders can reach without a prior visa, whether visa-free or on arrival. It was first launched in 2006 and is published by a London-based firm. NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index, now in its fourth edition, assesses how ready Indian states and union territories are to export. It is organised around four pillars: export infrastructure, business ecosystem, policy and governance, and export performance. The index supports India's goal of reaching one trillion dollars in merchandise exports by 2030.

questions.q: What percentage weight does the business ecosystem pillar carry in NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The business ecosystem pillar carries a 40 per cent weight, the largest of the four pillars.

questions.q: Singapore tops the Henley Passport Index 2026; how many countries does its passport give access to without a prior visa? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Singapore retained the top position with access to 192 countries.

questions.q: Which country tied with Japan for second place in the Henley Passport Index 2026?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Japan and South Korea are tied for second place.

questions.q: Food prices entered deflation for the first time since which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet says food prices entered deflation at -0.2% for the first time since 2014.

questions.q: In which year is India projected to surpass Germany to become the third-largest economy? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet projects India to surpass Germany by 2027.

questions.q: What is India's rank in per capita nominal GDP? (rank number)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives India's per capita nominal GDP as $2,820, ranked 136th.

questions.q: Which large state is named first in the 'Leaders' category of the Export Preparedness Index?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra is listed first among the large-state leaders, followed by Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.
